answer: Opal-spectrum voyage proof: one $29 UV torch and one $18 opal cabochon buys a single identity. At each epoch the holder shines the torch on the stone while the registry auditor matches its fluorescence spectrum against the certificate filed in the public gem registry — a forged stone fails to match the recorded curve and is rejected outright. The stone also travels: every epoch it is photographed at a new named meadow waypoint, so a reused photo shows yesterday's waypoint and exposes the copy. Each stone vouches for exactly one identity, and a spectrum cannot be photocopied.
